stances.claim: The Supreme Court properly held that the Comelec gravely abused its discretion in ruling Poe was not a natural-born citizen, that she failed the 10-year residency, and that she made false material representations -- 'deadly diseased with grave abuse of discretion from root to fruits' because the rulings violated the Constitution, the OEC, and settled jurisprudence; grave abuse exists in two ways (actual lack/excess of jurisdiction; virtual lack/excess via whimsy/arbitrariness/despotism).
stances.rhetorical_move: doctrine-application framing (two-way grave abuse + 'deadly diseased' characterization)

stances.claim: The OEC grants Comelec authority to cancel COCs 'exclusively' on the ground of material/false/deliberately-deceiving misrepresentation -- and the Comelec's veering into citizenship and residency rulings 'usurped a power vested solely in the Court' under the Constitution: 'The Supreme Court, sitting en banc, shall be the sole judge of all contests relating to the qualifications of the President.'

Poe as a foundling found in the Philippines is presumed a natural-born citizen due to the statistical fact that 'over 99 percent of babies born here have Filipino parents,' and critics challenging this carry the burden of proving alien parentage (which they 'utterly failed to discharge'); the presumption is strengthened by Poe's 'typical Filipino features: height, flat nasal bridge, straight black hair, almond shaped eyes and an oval face,' and the 1935 Constitution's silence on foundlings was framer-intended as inclusion, not exclusion.

Poe's residency claim is correct -- 10 years 11 months on the day before the 2016 elections -- because she 'decided to permanently abandon her U.S. residence' and 'actually re-established her residence here on 24 May 2005'; coupled with reacquisition application and family's continuous PH stay, her May 24, 2005 return 'was for good,' making her COC statements truthful and not deliberately deceptive.

Critics claim only seven justices upheld natural-born/residency (with Caguioa-Peralta concurring only on grave abuse and Del Castillo dissenting without voting on citizenship), so Poe's qualifications can be challenged again if she wins -- but CJ Sereno correctly noted that 'seven is a clear majority of the justices who actually voted on these issues,' and anyone can sue anyone in our litigious society (Duterte, Binay, Roxas, etc.) -- but 'suing is one thing; winning is quite another.'

The losers 'should stop whining' -- they have 'put up a good fight and there is honor in defeat. The Court has spoken. Let us respect its final verdict' -- making the column an explicit civic-respect plea to those who opposed Poe.

Poe's preserved feature-description: 'typical Filipino features: height, flat nasal bridge, straight black hair, almond shaped eyes and an oval face' -- using physical-anthropological evidence as supplementary presumption-strengthener.
Comelec's 'arrogantly' ignored repatriation jurisprudence -- a single-adverb editorial judgment doing significant work.
Poe's May 24, 2005 return 'was for good' -- using the colloquial-finality phrase to settle the residency question with everyday weight.
Sereno's plurality-vs-majority defense: 'seven is a clear majority of the justices who actually voted on these issues' -- clean arithmetical defense against critics' procedural complaint.

The litigious-society catalog: 'anyone can challenge Poe's qualifications in case she wins, in the same manner that anyone can contest the eligibility of, say, Rodrigo Duterte whose disqualification suit is still pending in the Comelec, or of Jejomar Binay, who may be sued for alleged corruption, or of Mar Roxas in the same way he filed a protest against Binay's vice-presidential victory in 2010.' -- using three named precedents to physicalize universal-suing reality.
The 'suing is one thing; winning is quite another' aphorism -- CJ's clean parallel-construction inversion separating standing from merit.

The closing civic-respect plea: 'The losers should stop whining. They have put up a good fight and there is honor in defeat. The Court has spoken. Let us respect its final verdict.' -- direct address to defeated parties.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban explains the Supreme Court's denial with finality (same 9-6 vote) of the motions for reconsideration on its decision allowing Grace Poe to run for President. The 47-page decision was 'superbly penned by Justice Jose Portugal Perez,' though five concurring and five dissenting opinions plus the decision (excluding separate opinions on MRs) total 688 single-spaced pages. The gut issue: did the Comelec gravely abuse its discretion in holding (1) Poe is not a natural-born citizen, (2) she failed the 10-year residency, and (3) she made false material representations in her COC? Grave abuse of discretion has two forms -- actual lack/excess of jurisdiction, and virtual lack/excess via whimsical, arbitrary, or despotic conduct. The Court held the Comelec rulings 'deadly diseased with grave abuse of discretion from root to fruits' for violating Constitution, OEC, and settled jurisprudence. The OEC grants Comelec authority to cancel COCs 'exclusively' on the ground that a material representation is false and made with deliberate intent to mislead the electorate; veering from this ground to rule on natural-born citizenship and residency, the Comelec usurped a power vested solely in the Court ('The Supreme Court, sitting en banc, shall be the sole judge of all contests relating to the qualifications of the President'). As a newborn foundling found in the Philippines, Poe is presumed a natural-born citizen because 'over 99 percent of babies born here have Filipino parents'; critics carry the burden of proving alien parentage and 'utterly failed to discharge' it. The presumption is strengthened by Poe's 'typical Filipino features: height, flat nasal bridge, straight black hair, almond shaped eyes and an oval face.' The 1935 Constitution's silence on foundlings has 'no restrictive language which would definitely exclude foundlings either,' and framers 'intended foundlings to be covered by the enumeration.' Social justice + equal protection favor foundlings; domestic adoption laws and generally-accepted international law principles obligate PH to grant nationality from birth. The Comelec 'arrogantly' ignored settled jurisprudence that repatriation restores natural-born status. As to residency, Poe's claim of 10 years 11 months on the day before the 2016 elections 'is true': she 'decided to permanently abandon her U.S. residence' and 'actually re-established her residence here on 24 May 2005,' which coupled with her reacquisition application and family's continuous PH stay shows her return 'was for good.' Her COC statements were therefore neither false nor deliberately deceptive. Justice Caguioa, joined by Justice Peralta, concurred on grave abuse but found voting on citizenship/residency unnecessary; Justice Del Castillo dissented but did not vote on citizenship. Critics claim only seven justices upheld natural-born/residency, leaving Poe's qualifications challengeable if she wins; CJ Sereno correctly pointed out that 'seven is a clear majority of the justices who actually voted on these issues.' Anyone can sue anyone in PH's litigious society -- Duterte (Comelec disqualification suit pending), Binay (alleged corruption), Roxas (2010 VP protest precedent against Binay) -- but 'suing is one thing; winning is quite another.' Meanwhile, the losers 'should stop whining. They have put up a good fight and there is honor in defeat. The Court has spoken. Let us respect its final verdict.'
